claims.text: Pt, Ir, or Ru salts reduce before Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe salts at temperatures below 300°C.
Early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru establishes a noble-metal lattice.
The nascent noble-metal surface promotes hydrogen adsorption and dissociation.
Reactive hydrogen atoms generated on the noble-metal surface reduce adjacent Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe species.
The reduced less-noble metals integrate into the pre-existing noble-metal lattice.
Noble-metal-templated hydrogen reduction ensures formation of a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Spray drying homogeneously mixed aqueous salts produces near-spherical and compositionally uniform precursor particles.
The resulting HEA material forms a porous, self-supported three-dimensional nanoframework assembled from nanoarms.
The resulting nanoframework has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Pt–Ru materials initially retain Pt-based fcc domains.
Secondary heating overcomes an approximately 0.45 eV kinetic barrier for an fcc-to-hcp transformation in Pt–Ru materials.
The Ru-based hcp phase is thermodynamically more stable than the initially formed Pt-based fcc phase in the relevant Pt–Ru systems.
Increasing Ru content and applying secondary heating increase the Ru-hcp phase fraction.
The balance between Pt-based fcc and Ru-based hcp domains governs or tunes methanol oxidation performance.
PtNiCoCuRuIr HEA-3DNFs will have substantially higher methanol-oxidation mass activity than commercial Pt black and Pt-rich PtNiCoCuRu reduced only at 300°C.
PtNiCoCuRuIr HEA-3DNFs will sustain higher methanol-oxidation current than the stated baselines.
The predicted catalytic enhancement arises from higher electrochemically active surface area and optimized phase composition.
Commercial Johnson Matthey Pt black has a methanol-oxidation mass activity of 170 mA/mgPt and an electrochemically active surface area of 17.59 m2/gPt under the relevant comparison conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies from 300°C to 500°C for homogeneously mixed precursors containing Pt, Ir, or Ru under hydrogen reduction and, for Pt–Ru variation, over Pt:Ru ratios from 3:1 to 1:4.
The proposed mechanism does not apply to Pd-based or noble-metal-free systems because differing reduction kinetics or phase separation dominate.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says templated reduction ensures a homogeneous single-phase solid solution, whereas the structural mediator invokes coexistence of distinct Pt-based fcc and Ru-based hcp domains. Coexisting fcc and hcp domains ordinarily describe a multiphase or multidomain structure unless a specific distinction between the general HEA and the Pt–Ru subseries is made.
